title: Stem soft rot disease in outdoor tomatoes

Header: Stem soft rot disease in outdoor tomatoes

Prevention: Prevention
This disease can only be managed by using a combination of measures.
If fungicide-treated seeds are available, use them.
Do not treat seeds yourself .
Do not use treated seeds as food or feed.Select nursery site away from tomato, potato, all type of peppers, egg plants, night shade, onions.
Avoid fields with history of stem rot.
Keep wide plant spacing (>60 cm, 25”) to allow good aeration.
Remove lower leaves from the plants and use staking to increase aeration.
Rotate tomatoes with non-susceptible crops, e.g. maize, in 3-season breaks.
This disease lives in the soil and in many crops, e.g. tomato, spinach, onion, okra, sunflower, cabbages
Avoid frequent irrigation and water logging.
Do not irrigate in evenings.
Use furrow irrigation instead of sprinkler irrigation to reduce chances for disease spread.
Be aware that this disease can be spread with seeds, by farm equipment, by animals or with water.
Fungal spores can be carried with winds.
You may partly prevent infection with spores of this fungus by using garlic sprays. (Finely chop 20 garlic cloves, soak 1 d in 100 ml mineral oil, then + 10 ml soap, stir, + 2 litre water, stir).
Then spray over entire plants.
Particularly spray the flowers.
Max 3 sprays per season.
Remove crop residues.
Monitoring: Stem rot, also called soft rot or
It affects tomato roots and stems at flowering and ripening stage.
Search for soft white fungal growth on the stems near the soil surface during wet weather.
It causes rapid wilting with no prior yellowing of the leaves.
When the first infected plant is detected, immediate action is suggested
Direct Control: It is easier to prevent this disease than to control it.
Remove infected plants with roots and surrounding soil and burn or bury everything deeply.
Do not re-plant tomatoes in the same spot for 3 seasons.

Restrictions
It is easier to prevent this disease than to control it.
There is no effective chemical control against the soil borne period of this disease.
Foliar application of fungicides can partly protect against further infection by spores of this disease.
It is effective only when ripen plant materials, such as flowers, are fully covered by the sprayed chemical.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
